description: Collecting locations over the phone: city, country, neighbourhood, pickup point, service, delivery and billing addresses, landmarks, floors and unit numbers. Most of these are whole-word values that a caller will correct instantly if the agent gets them wrong, so they settle inside the next question. A full postal address is the exception: it gets one consolidated readback at the end with the postcode or zip read character by character, in both labels.

subtle: Echo-and-advance is the default: fold the line just given into the next question.
Collect the whole address first, then read it back once, cleanly, at the end.
Standalone city, country, neighbourhood and landmark settle inside the next question, no round trip.
Bare value-as-question for short corrections: Three B, thanks.
Silent accept when the caller stated it twice or emphatically.
Postcode or zip in the final readback is always character by character.
First word of an agent turn never repeats consecutively and rarely at all; value-first openers.
Check tags (right? yeah? correct?) at most twice per call; most fields carry no tag.
Contractions throughout, short clauses, commas not dashes.
No praise, no status phrases, no I heard, no chatbot closer.
non_subtle_tells: One identical template on every field: Just to confirm, X. Is that correct?
Every address line confirmed separately instead of one consolidated readback.
Praise on trivial answers, status phrases like I have recorded that.
No contractions, over-formal register, I will now proceed to.
Wrong direction: over-casual agent that skips the consolidated readback, drops the unit number, or mumbles the postcode as a whole word instead of character by character.
